## Adventures in Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, and Colombia: four different experiences

Our selection includes a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The four countries in this page's title are part of that route, not a separate four-country program. The journey passes through Chile between Argentina and Bolivia, and through Ecuador and the Galápagos between Peru and Colombia. The entire transport plan matters when choosing a trip.

The most demanding adventure section takes place in Bolivia by 4×4. Argentina offers walks near Iguazú Falls, Peru takes travelers through the Andes and to Machu Picchu, and Colombia includes a visit to El Peñón Rock. Physical demands vary: high altitude and long off-road drives are more challenging than ordinary walks through city streets.

## Bolivia: two days off-road in the highlands

After an acclimatization stop in San Pedro de Atacama, you cross the border between Chile and Bolivia. The [two-day Uyuni excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/) begins, visiting [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers, and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The night is spent at an expedition-style hotel.

On day two, you travel past small lagoons, the Ollagüe volcano area, the Chiguana Salt Flat, and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The itinerary includes stops at Colchani, Ojos de Agua, and an island with giant cacti. This is an expedition by vehicle; self-driving a jeep or undertaking a challenging sports trek is not listed.

Parts of the route exceed 4,000 meters. Altitude sickness is possible in the highlands. Good physical fitness does not guarantee easy acclimatization, so health and the rate of ascent must be considered beforehand. The expedition is followed by a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and then another high-altitude section in Peru.

## Argentina: walking routes around Iguazú Falls

The Argentine section includes a [waterfalls excursion](/argentina/puerto-iguazu/iguazu-argentina-group-russian-program/) from [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The national park visit focuses on maintained paths, views of the waterfalls, and tropical forest. A boat safari, rafting, or challenging trek is not confirmed as part of this particular excursion day.

Access to individual viewpoints depends on river levels. In 2026, the Argentine park authority reported restrictions affecting some walkways due to high water flow. Checking which routes are open is especially important: after the waterfalls you fly to Buenos Aires, with no extra day set aside to reschedule the walk.

## Peru: Titicaca, the Andean road, and Machu Picchu

From Bolivia, you enter Peru through Desaguadero. The itinerary features [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) with the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), followed by a daytime bus journey through Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, and the La Raya Pass to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is visited on a [one-day excursion from Cusco](/peru/cusco/machu-picchu-day-tour-from-cusco/) involving a train and an English-speaking guide. You will walk through the archaeological site, but **there is no multi-day Inca Trail trek**. Tickets are valid for a specified date, time, and sightseeing circuit. Adding a trek would require rearranging several days, not simply using a spare hour in Cusco.

## Colombia: El Peñón Rock and a walk through Guatapé

After the Peruvian section, the journey continues through Ecuador before arriving in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). An [excursion to El Peñol and Guatapé](/colombia/medellin/el-penol-guatape-from-medellin/) is included. A long staircase leads up [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), with views of the reservoir from the lookout. Check the particular offer for included admission tickets and any additional activities.

[Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) is also appealing for its streets and vividly painted decorative panels on the lower parts of buildings. The route then turns to cultural stops in Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá. No multi-day trekking, canyoning, or rafting in Colombia is listed for this program.

## Understanding the actual physical demands

| Section | What to expect |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | National park walkways |
| Bolivia | 4×4 travel and altitude |
| Peru | Mountain road journeys |
| Guatapé | Climbing stairs |

The overall 32-day route involves early starts, flights, hot lowlands, and cold highlands. Comfortable shoes, sun protection, and layered clothes matter more than technical mountaineering equipment, which is not included in the product.

If you are primarily interested in off-road journeys, compare [adventure tours featuring Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/). For a broader range of destinations, the [general Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, and Peru selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia_peru/) shows the combination without a thematic filter. Changing the countries requires recalculating transportation, overnight stays, and tickets.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure journeys

### Is trekking on the Inca Trail included?

No. Machu Picchu is visited on a day trip with train travel and a guided tour of the archaeological complex.

### Which section is the most difficult in terms of altitude?

The two-day Bolivian route includes areas above 4,000 meters. La Paz and the mountainous regions of Peru follow. Altitude sickness risk must be assessed individually.

### Can I travel only to the four countries in the title?

The available itinerary visits eight countries, including Chile and Ecuador between the featured sections. Shortening it means creating a different journey.

## Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, and Colombia: a journey across historical eras

On the [32-day tour of eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), these four countries offer a particularly compelling cultural story: the urban traditions of the Río de la Plata, the monuments of Tiwanaku, the heritage of the Incas, and Colombia's colonial cities. However, the four countries in the selection title are only part of a longer itinerary. Chile comes between Argentina and Bolivia, and Ecuador between Peru and Colombia. This catalog does not promise a separate, direct four-country trip.

The journey offers opportunities to compare civilizations that flourished centuries apart and see how urban culture evolved across the continent. To get the most from it, distinguish museum visits, archaeological experiences, and sections dominated by transportation.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires, its neighborhoods, and tango

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the itinerary includes a city tour with a Russian-speaking guide. Neighborhoods and landmarks include La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta, and Puerto Madero. Walking through the city reveals different periods of its development and daily life, from older neighborhoods to the former port area.

An evening [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-dinner-transfer/) is included. Here tango forms part of the city's cultural history rather than an incidental evening extra. The next day you travel to Uruguay, so the program does not include several days devoted to exploring Buenos Aires's museums and theaters.

If Argentine city experiences matter more to you than the other destinations, compare the available [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) by their duration and activities.

## Bolivia: La Paz and the Tiwanaku civilization

Bolivia's cultural section follows a journey through the lagoons and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). La Paz includes a city tour featuring historical landmarks and the Witches' Market.

The following day, the route leads to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) on the way toward the Peruvian border. It is the heritage of an independent pre-Columbian civilization that existed long before the Inca Empire reached its height. The excursion description mentions the Gateway of the Sun and Kalasasaya. Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu therefore should not be presented as two parts of the same Inca complex: they belong to different historical contexts.

The archaeological visits take place at considerable altitude after several days in Bolivia's highlands. Physical well-being and the time needed to travel onward to Peru remain important even if history is the journey's main purpose.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco, and Machu Picchu

After crossing near Desaguadero, travelers arrive at [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) introduces the traditional way of life of their inhabitants. The group then travels by tourist bus through Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, La Raya, and Pucará to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). This route is itself an introduction to several periods of Andean history, not just a transfer without stops.

A [Machu Picchu excursion](/peru/cusco/machu-picchu-day-tour-from-cusco/) from Cusco includes train travel and an English-speaking guide. The following day features Coricancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay, and Sacsayhuamán. Travelers then fly to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) for a city tour that includes its historic center and Miraflores.

A ticket to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is issued for a particular date, time, and circuit through the site. The visit therefore cannot simply be moved to make room for an additional walk in Cusco without coordinating tickets and flights. If Inca history is your main interest, compare the [cultural and historical tours featuring Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/) by the time allocated to archaeological sites.

## Colombia: from Comuna 13 to Cartagena and Bogotá

The group reaches Colombia only after Ecuador, flying to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A city tour includes an introduction to [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). This neighborhood reveals contemporary urban culture and art that differ markedly from the ancient monuments of the Andes.

The next major cultural destination is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The itinerary includes a tour of its historic city and San Felipe Fortress, linked to the Caribbean coast's colonial era.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), a [city tour](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/) is planned, covering La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero Collection, and Monserrate. A separate day is dedicated to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. The Colombian portion thus combines colonial neighborhoods, art, and stories of modern city life.

Pay attention to museum closing days: the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Casa de Moneda and Botero Collection are closed on Tuesdays. If the order of visits changes, these restrictions should be checked against the calendar.

## Comparing the four cultural sections

| Country | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Tango and neighborhoods |
| Bolivia | Tiwanaku |
| Peru | Inca heritage |
| Colombia | Cities and museums |

The value of this route lies in its contrasting eras and traditions, but experiencing them requires time for flights and borders. The journey from Peru to Colombia, for example, is not direct: Quito and the Galápagos lie between them in the full itinerary. Travelers who want to explore one civilization in depth may gain more time at its monuments on a shorter specialist tour.

For history-focused choices, explore [cultural tours featuring Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/) and [Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/). The [general selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia_peru/) also contains all current itineraries passing through these four countries.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural itinerary

### Do Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu belong to the same civilization?

No. Tiwanaku is a monument of an independent pre-Columbian Andean culture, while Machu Picchu is associated with the Inca civilization. Visiting both helps illustrate the differences between historical periods.

### Can we explore all Bogotá's museums in depth in one day?

The confirmed itinerary includes a busy sightseeing day but does not promise several days of museum visits. Additional visits require extra time and checks of each institution's opening days.

### Are other countries included beyond the four listed?

Yes. The complete journey covers eight countries. The cultural visits in these four are interspersed with further stages in Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, and Ecuador.

## Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, and Peru: from humid forest to Andean peaks

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including [Argentina](/argentina/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Colombia](/colombia/), and [Peru](/peru/). All four are part of the [32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), which also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, and Ecuador. Neither the number of borders nor the order of countries in the catalog title substitutes for the actual day-by-day itinerary.

The chief reason to choose this combination for nature is the contrast between Iguazú's humid lowland forest and the highlands of Bolivia and Peru. In southwestern Bolivia, salt lakes, volcanic areas, and Uyuni shape the landscape. Peru adds the waters of Titicaca and the steep green slopes surrounding Machu Picchu. Colombia's Guatapé provides a shorter but memorable scenic stop.

## The Argentine side of Iguazú: water and subtropical forest

[Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) appears early in the journey. You arrive after visiting the waterfalls on the Brazilian side and take a guided tour of the Argentine national park routes with a Russian-speaking guide. A flight to Buenos Aires follows. This schedule allows you to compare both sides of the waterfalls but leaves limited time for extra nature excursions beyond those listed.

Iguazú Falls are set within protected subtropical forest. UNESCO recognizes the natural significance of the Argentine park and its transboundary relationship with the Brazilian park. From the walkways, you can see different sections of the cascades, clouds of spray, and green riverbanks. No dedicated jungle trek or guaranteed wildlife observation is scheduled for this day.

The remainder of the Argentine portion includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), sightseeing, and tango. The route then proceeds through Uruguay and Chile, so several busy transport and city days separate Iguazú from Bolivia's lagoons.

## Bolivia: lagoons, the Dalí Desert, and two days by jeep

The Bolivian nature section begins after San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. You spend two days traveling across the Altiplano in 4×4 vehicles with an English-speaking guide.

Day one includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), Licancabur Volcano, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geyser area, and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Day two features a chain of high-altitude lagoons, Ollagüe Volcano, the Chiguana Salt Flat, and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Stops include Colchani, Ojos de Agua, and an island with giant cacti.

The landscape demands preparation: parts of the road lie above 4,000 m, the overnight stay is in an expedition hotel, and jeeps are used on sections without ordinary paved roads. An acclimatization stop is already built into the itinerary before entering Bolivia. Temperature, road conditions, and participants' well-being matter more than trying to recreate a photograph of Uyuni's mirror effect, which depends on the season and rainfall.

After the expedition, you fly from Uyuni to La Paz. That means moving into another high-altitude section rather than returning to sea level.

## Peru: crossing the border to Titicaca and traveling to Machu Picchu

The journey enters Peru through Desaguadero after La Paz and Tiwanaku. The first major nature stop is [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), with an excursion to the Uros Islands. The lake experience contrasts sharply with Bolivia's dry salt flats: a high-altitude body of water, island communities, and broad open waters.

The next day involves a tourist bus to Cusco with stops along the way, followed by an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The archaeological site is visited in a group with an English-speaking guide, returning to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) by train. UNESCO notes that the historical complex sits in a mountainous landscape where the Andes meet the upper Amazon, and that its natural surroundings form part of the site's significance.

On this itinerary, Machu Picchu is primarily an archaeological excursion set against dramatic mountain scenery. **A multi-day Inca Trail hike is not included**, nor is a separate expedition into the Amazon rainforest. In practice, discuss ordinary walking requirements and altitude tolerance in advance rather than treating every archaeological stop as a nature trek.

After Cusco, the itinerary includes a flight and city sightseeing in Lima before continuing to Ecuador. Bolivia and Peru therefore appear **consecutively** on the actual route, unlike Colombia, which comes near the end of the longer journey.

## Colombia: El Peñón and Guatapé, followed by cities

One day in the Colombian section is especially appealing to landscape enthusiasts: an excursion from [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The rock and reservoir, with its branching bays, form a recognizable landscape, while climbing to the lookout requires significant effort from the legs. Colombia's official tourism portal separately describes the ascent and the panorama from the monolith.

The rest of the Colombian itinerary includes city sightseeing in Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá, plus visits to Monserrate and Zipaquirá. These stops are notable for culture, architecture, and views, but the program does not include a dedicated national-park trek or a separate Colombian Amazon nature expedition.

## Comparing nature days and physical demands

| Section | What is planned | What to consider |
|---|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazú waterfall walkways | Humidity, walking, and a flight after the excursion |
| Bolivia | 2 days by 4×4 through lagoons and Uyuni | Altitude over 4,000 m, cold, long drives |
| Peru | Titicaca, Machu Picchu, Cusco | High-altitude transfers, walking, and train travel |
| Colombia | El Peñón and Guatapé | Climb to the lookout and further city days |

The complete tour lasts 32 days, with its 2026 dates set from October 22 to November 22. International air travel is not included in the price; domestic flights form part of the agreed itinerary. Travelers must account for transfers across all eight countries, including those omitted from this filter's title. Before departure, current entry requirements, travel restrictions, access to highland regions, and tickets for the Machu Picchu railway section should be confirmed.

For another combination, explore the [multi-country nature tours](/multi-country/interests/nature/). All programs featuring this geography without a thematic filter are available in the [Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, and Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia_peru/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Bolivia and Peru visited one after the other?

Yes. After the Bolivian section, you travel through Tiwanaku and Desaguadero to Puno, then continue toward Cusco and Machu Picchu.

### Does this tour include hiking the Inca Trail?

No. A one-day visit to Machu Picchu with sightseeing and a return by train is scheduled. A full multi-day trek would require a different itinerary.

### What does Colombia offer to nature-focused travelers?

The main confirmed scenic stop is El Peñón and Guatapé. The remainder of the Colombian section features cities and cultural attractions.

### Can I book this as a ready-made four-country journey?

No. This catalog filters one long eight-country product. A journey limited to the selected countries would require a separately agreed itinerary.

## Nature and wildlife in Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, and Colombia: what you can actually experience

This selection relates to the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Among the four countries named, nature is most prominent around Iguazú Falls and Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. Peru adds Lake Titicaca and the Andes; Colombia adds the hills and reservoir near Guatapé. The full journey has two separate themes: Nature for landscapes and Wildlife and Safari for fauna observation. **Having both themes on the overall tour does not mean that organized wildlife watching is included in every country**.

A significant island nature section of the complete itinerary takes place in the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, which is not among the countries named in this selection. If wildlife is your main reason for traveling, compare the actual excursion days rather than counting countries with beautiful landscapes.

## Argentina: Iguazú and the rainforest

On the Argentine side of the waterfalls, a [group excursion from Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/puerto-iguazu/iguazu-argentina-group-russian-program/) is scheduled. In the national park, you observe powerful cascades and tropical forest from specially built walking paths and viewpoints.

Many bird and mammal species inhabit the Iguazú area, but the waterfall excursion **is not a guaranteed safari**. A dedicated search for jaguars, nocturnal wildlife watching, or a separate birdwatching program is not listed for this Argentine day. The landscape and ecosystem are the confirmed reasons for visiting; sightings of particular animals cannot be promised.

Some park sections temporarily close when river levels are high. In 2026, the national park authority reported restrictions affecting access to certain walkways. Check which paths are actually available on the date of your visit.

## Bolivia: lagoons, flamingos, and salt flats

The most specific birdwatching opportunity among the four selected countries is associated with the [two-day Uyuni jeep tour](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/). The route passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), geothermal areas, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), and other high-altitude bodies of water. The standalone excursion description mentions James's flamingos near Laguna Colorada.

The format remains an expedition-style sightseeing journey: the group travels by jeep among several attractions over two days. Extended stationary observations with an ornithologist and guaranteed encounters with particular birds are not confirmed. Whether birds are present depends on season and natural conditions.

You then visit the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Colchani, and an island with giant cacti. The contrast with humid, tropical Iguazú is striking: dry highlands, lagoons, and a vast salt plain. This is a rewarding route for landscape photography, but it requires adapting to elevations above 4,000 meters.

## Peru: Titicaca and mountain ecosystems between cultural sites

After Bolivia, the itinerary leads to [Lake Titicaca near Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) with a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), then across the La Raya Pass to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Mountain valleys and high-altitude scenery feature along the way.

Next come [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the historical sights of Cusco and Lima. Although Machu Picchu is surrounded by rich natural ecosystems and is protected as a mixed natural and cultural area, this tour's visit focuses on archaeology. No dedicated wildlife photography excursion, condor search, or expedition into the Amazon rainforest is listed for the Peruvian days.

This distinction matters: Peru complements Bolivia for travelers who want to see Andean landscapes. Those seeking specialist wildlife observation should choose an itinerary with confirmed visits to natural habitats and time specifically allocated to them.

## Colombia: the Guatapé reservoir without promises of a safari

The Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and includes an [excursion to El Peñol and Guatapé](/colombia/medellin/el-penol-guatape-from-medellin/). The itinerary mentions [El Peñón Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and reservoirs surrounded by green hills; a separate ascent to the summit is not promised. [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) is also known for the colorful painted decoration of its buildings.

This is a scenic and cultural day. Separate excursions into Colombian rainforests, birdwatching for rare species, or marine wildlife outings are not included. Cartagena, Bogotá, and Zipaquirá follow, with predominantly historical and urban attractions.

## Where the substantial island nature experience takes place

After Peru and before reaching Colombia, you visit the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador. The itinerary includes Santa Cruz and **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour with Bachas Beach, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The actual branch is confirmed at booking; the program does not include both simultaneously.

The Galápagos are an important part of the full journey for travelers interested in island ecosystems. Geographically, however, they are not in Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, or Colombia. If wildlife is the main goal, compare the [themed tours featuring Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) and the complete itinerary rather than judging only this four-country selection's title.

## Comparing the nature experiences correctly

| Place | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | Waterfalls and forest |
| Laguna Colorada | High-altitude birds |
| Titicaca | Lake and culture |
| Guatapé | Hills and reservoir |

The itinerary offers diverse opportunities to photograph waterfalls and mountains. Photographing a particular animal species requires information on the observation site, time of day, season, and length of the stop; a country list provides none of these. For more choices, explore [nature trips](/interests/nature/) featuring waterfalls and mountain scenery, [Wildlife and Safari tours](/interests/wildlife/) featuring fauna observation, or the [general four-country combination](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia_peru/).

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife watching

### Is it guaranteed that we will see flamingos in Bolivia?

No. The excursion visits Laguna Colorada, and the description mentions flamingos, but actual sightings depend on natural conditions.

### Can we see jaguars on the Iguazú excursion?

The excursion focuses on waterfalls and park walks. There is no dedicated jaguar search or guaranteed encounter.

### Are the Galápagos part of this four-country geography?

No. They are in Ecuador, but they are included in the complete 32-day eight-country itinerary represented by this selection.

## Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Colombia: what lies between them

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. We offer the [32-day Eight Countries of South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The itinerary starts in Brazil, continues through Argentina and Uruguay, then Chile, Bolivia, Peru, and Ecuador, and ends in Colombia. This selection highlights four countries along the complete route.

The appeal lies in the contrast between travel experiences. [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) offers city walks and tango, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) a trip across the Río de la Plata, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) off-road journeys and salt flats, and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) two very different sides of Colombia. But these stops receive different amounts of time: Uruguay is visited in a single day, whereas Bolivia and Colombia each occupy several consecutive days.

## Uruguay: a day trip from Buenos Aires

In the Argentine capital, travelers have a city tour and an evening tango show with dinner. The following day is dedicated to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). According to the itinerary, participants leave early for the port, cross the Río de la Plata by ferry, explore Uruguay's capital with an English-speaking guide, enjoy some free time, and return to Buenos Aires. Ferry tickets are included.

The important distinction is that **Uruguay does not involve a separate multi-day stay on this tour**. Considerably less time is spent in Montevideo than in Buenos Aires, and participants return to their hotel in Argentina after the ferry crossing. If the aim is a deeper exploration of Uruguay, compare [Uruguay tours](/uruguay/tour/) for overnight stays, other cities, or wine-producing regions.

The ferry crossing is an international journey. Entry rules for Uruguay and re-entry into Argentina, passport validity, and the carrier's requirements must be checked for each nationality. Allowing time for check-in and border formalities matters more here than simply estimating the distance between the two capitals.

## Why the itinerary does not go directly from Uruguay to Bolivia

After returning to Buenos Aires, the program continues with a flight to Santiago, Chile, then onward to Calama and San Pedro de Atacama. Only then does the Bolivian 4×4 section begin. It crosses Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, geothermal areas, colorful lagoons, and salt flats on the way to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). An overnight expedition stay and further travel are followed by a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/).

This is a major change from ferry crossings and city excursions to remote high-altitude roads. Our tour includes sections above 4,000 m, with a risk of altitude sickness. Warm clothing, wind and sun protection, a comfortable daypack for personal belongings, and careful consideration of altitude tolerance are important. The guide on the journey toward Uyuni speaks English; the guide languages in other cities depend on the specific excursions.

Adding Bolivia to a trip through Argentina and Uruguay therefore means adding not only another country, but also a Chilean transport sequence involving flights and an overland mountain border crossing.

## Colombia comes only after Peru and Ecuador

After Bolivia, the itinerary continues to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Travelers then visit Quito, the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), and Guayaquil. They fly to Colombia from Guayaquil. Describing the four selected countries must therefore not suggest a direct La Paz–Bogotá flight or a transfer from Uyuni to Cartagena.

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary includes an excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and an introduction to Comuna 13. The route then continues to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) with its Salt Cathedral. This is a substantial final section, not a short airport connection in Colombia.

The climate changes again during the Colombian section: after the warm Caribbean coast, travelers return to a high-altitude city. Plan clothing and carry-on luggage for the entire journey, not just its warmest part.

## What changes in documents and budgeting

There are at least two fundamentally different border-crossing scenarios: **a sea journey from Argentina to Uruguay and back**, and **an overland high-altitude entry into Bolivia from Chile**. The full itinerary also includes international flights. Before booking, check each traveler's passport requirements, permitted length of stay, re-entry rules, transit requirements, and carrier conditions. Visa-free entry to one country does not automatically apply to its neighbors.

Russian citizens are included on Colombia's official list of nationalities that do not need a tourist visa for short visits, although entry remains subject to the immigration authorities' decision. Entry requirements for Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, and Ecuador must also be checked for the particular traveler's nationality and route.

The four highlighted sections use the Argentine peso, Uruguayan peso, boliviano, and Colombian peso. Further stops on the full tour add several more currencies. Exchange options and international card acceptance depend on current restrictions, the country, and the bank. Ada Tours helps travelers separate included services, independent purchases, and reserve funds without promising that any particular card will work at every stop.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, and Uruguay

### How many days are spent in Uruguay?

On our tour, Uruguay is a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, returning the same day. No overnight stay in Uruguay is scheduled.

### Can we go directly from Montevideo to Uyuni?

That is not part of this itinerary. Between Montevideo and Uyuni, the journey involves returning to Argentina, flights through Chile, and an overland high-altitude expedition.

### Why does a tour featuring four selected countries last so long?

Because the actual product visits eight countries, includes major sections in Peru and Ecuador, and uses several forms of transport. A dedicated four-country itinerary would have to be planned differently.

### Where is the risk of altitude-related discomfort greatest?

On the Bolivian mountain section, with locations above 4,000 m. The preceding city visits do not replace acclimatization; medical considerations should be assessed before departure.
